title: Issue 19 Autumn 2006 Newsletter of the Drug Misuse Research Division: drugnet Ireland
extended_summary:
This paper is a newsletter issue from Drugnet Ireland that summarizes a range of drug- and alcohol-related policy, surveillance, and service updates in Ireland. It does not examine K-12 science learning or any educational technology intervention. Instead, it reports on topics such as outcomes from the ROSIE opiate treatment study, drug-related prosecutions and seizures, driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol, drug treatment and rehabilitation policy, peer drugs education, helpline trends, and regional task-force planning.

The issue compiles brief articles by different authors and draws on existing reports, administrative data, and monitoring systems rather than presenting a single empirical intervention study. The one item with an educational component describes a peer drugs education programme in Kilkenny, where older secondary students were trained to deliver drugs education to younger students in school settings. That section emphasizes program description and recognition rather than a rigorous evaluation.

Overall, the issue’s main conclusions are that opiate treatment was associated with improved outcomes for adult users, drug driving remained a significant concern, policy structures in Ireland were increasingly organized around integrated drug and alcohol responses, and peer-led drug education was viewed as a promising approach. Because the text is a newsletter and not a controlled study, it provides descriptive evidence and policy commentary rather than causal evaluation.
quality_tier_rationale: This is grey-literature newsletter content summarizing policy and public-health reports, not a peer-reviewed study with a clear analytic design. It does not evaluate an educational intervention or report a formal methodology relevant to K-12 science learning evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has no direct impact on K-12 science learning outcomes, mechanisms, or educational technology. Its content is unrelated to the requested domain and provides no measurable educational effect.
